cards.front: Define the absolute value of a real number $x$, denoted $|x|$.
cards.back: $$|x| = \begin{cases} x & \text{if } x \ge 0 \\ -x & \text{if } x < 0 \end{cases}$$ Intuitively, $|x|$ represents the distance of $x$ from zero on the number line, which is always non-negative.

cards.front: How do you solve an absolute value equation of the form $|X| = a$, where $a \ge 0$?
cards.back: If $a \ge 0$, then $X = a$ or $X = -a$. For example, if $|x|=5$, then $x=5$ or $x=-5$. If $a < 0$, there is no solution.

cards.front: How do you solve an absolute value inequality of the form $|X| < a$, where $a > 0$?
cards.back: If $a > 0$, then $-a < X < a$. This means $X$ is between $-a$ and $a$. For example, if $|x|<3$, then $-3 < x < 3$. If $a \le 0$, there is no solution.

cards.front: How do you solve an absolute value inequality of the form $|X| > a$, where $a \ge 0$?
cards.back: If $a \ge 0$, then $X < -a$ or $X > a$. This means $X$ is outside the interval $[-a, a]$. For example, if $|x| \ge 4$, then $x \le -4$ or $x \ge 4$. If $a < 0$, the solution is all real numbers.

This implies $2x-1 = 7$ or $2x-1 = -7$.
*   $2x = 8 \implies x = 4$
*   $2x = -6 \implies x = -3$
The solutions are $x=4$ and $x=-3$.

This implies $-5 < 3x+2 < 5$.
*   Subtract 2 from all parts: $-5-2 < 3x < 5-2 \implies -7 < 3x < 3$.
*   Divide by 3: $-7/3 < x < 1$.
The solution in interval notation is $(-7/3, 1)$.

This implies $5-x \ge 2$ or $5-x \le -2$.
*   $5-x \ge 2 \implies -x \ge -3 \implies x \le 3$
*   $5-x \le -2 \implies -x \le -7 \implies x \ge 7$
The solution is $x \le 3$ or $x \ge 7$. In interval notation: $(-\infty, 3] \cup [7, \infty)$.

Squaring both sides is a general method:
$(x+1)^2 = (2x-3)^2$
$x^2+2x+1 = 4x^2-12x+9$
$0 = 3x^2-14x+8$
Factor: $0 = (3x-2)(x-4)$
Thus, $3x-2=0 \implies x=2/3$ or $x-4=0 \implies x=4$.

cards.front: Explain the conditions for no solution for $|ax+b|=c$ and $|ax+b|<c$.
cards.back:
*   For $|ax+b|=c$: No solution if $c < 0$, because an absolute value cannot be negative.
*   For $|ax+b|<c$: No solution if $c \le 0$. If $c < 0$, an absolute value cannot be less than a negative number. If $c=0$, $|ax+b|<0$ has no solution as absolute value is always non-negative.
